text:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx error rate observed on /v1/generate (source: edge-proxy). Auto-created incident thread. Paging oncall now.

sam (oncall): seeing it, getting paged. investigating. :eyes:

lin (obs): heads-up — our Datadog intake shows a gap in metric/trace ingestion starting ~12:42 UTC, many dashboards are stale for the window. Could be vendor delay, not backend yet.

sam (oncall): checking app logs and k8s — I can still see request failures in app logs, will check code path. If DD is delayed we may not have traces for root cause.

jules (sre): if Datadog is behind we should enable local fallback metrics/long-term buffer and switch critical alerts to CloudWatch/prometheus-scrape temporarily.

ops-automation: datadog-status-bot posted: <https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/9abcde> "Investigating: Ingestion backlog impacting metrics and traces"

sam (oncall): thx. sam -> @priya: if I need to hand off, I'll call you in 20.

lin (obs): I'm seeing metric arrival latency spikes and a backlog in Datadog ingestion topic. UI timestamps show events queued but not indexed. This will create an observability blindspot for ~10-20m window unless we take action.

jules (sre): action plan: 1) flip critical alerts to fallback data (prometheus pushgateway / cloudwatch) 2) enable log sampling to send full request ids to S3 (for postmortem) 3) contact Datadog support and record incident id 4) track customer-facing impact and update status page

support-ops: customers are starting to message support about "no errors visible" in dashboards. Need a short status blurb if we confirm DD impact.

sam (oncall): quick checks: curl internal health looks fine for most services, but generate endpoint is returning 502s for some requests. App logs:

```
kubectl -n prod logs deploy/llm-api -c app --tail 200 | grep "5.." | head
2024-07-12T12:43:05Z ERROR request_id=abcd1234 upstream returned 502
2024-07-12T12:43:09Z ERROR request_id=abcd5678 downstream timeout
```

sam (oncall): so errors are real. We need tracing to know if it's model backend or proxy. With DD delayed, traces may be missing for 12:42-12:50.

lin (obs): runbook snippet to re-route alerts (copy/paste):

```
# temp route alerts to fallback
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_API_TOKEN" \
  https://console.redwood.ai/api/alerts/temporary_route \
  -d '{"route":"cloudwatch","alert_list":["generate-latency","generate-5xx"]}'
```

lin (obs): I've executed the route change for generate-5xx -> cloudwatch fallback. Confirming alerts are firing there. :white_check_mark:

ops-automation: started a buffered log forwarder job to S3 for request_ids in the 12:40-12:50 window. Job id: s3-forward-4421.

datadog-status-bot: UPDATE: Ingestion backlog persists; team investigating consumer throughput issues. Incident link: <https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/9abcde/updates>

jules (sre): contacting Datadog support with our incident details (include queued events count + example trace ids). Priya, I'm going to handoff to you in ~10 if you can take oncall.

priya (handoff): standing by, will take over at 12:55 UTC if needed.

sam (oncall): handoff to @priya: logs + temp alert routing done, buffering started, contacting datadog. I'm going offline for urgent meeting in 5. Priya, own the incident, pls post updates to status.redwood.ai and coord with support.

priya (handoff): taking over. Severity bumped to Sev2 (customer-facing errors, partial outage for generate). Updating incident header and pinging account teams.

priya (handoff): quick customer blurb draft: "We are investigating increased errors for the 'generate' API. Our telemetry provider is experiencing ingestion delays which temporarily limits visibility; we have routed critical alerts to fallback systems and are actively mitigating. More updates soon." Thoughts?

support-ops: good short blurb. Add recommended workaround: retry with exponential backoff.

priya (handoff): published to status.redwood.ai and notified top 5 affected customers via secure channel.

lin (obs): created a synthetic check to validate end-to-end generation every 30s and alert to fallback. Also saved a snapshot of the incomplete traces we have for 12:40-12:48 for postmortem.

jules (sre): Datadog replied: investigating internal consumer saturation, recommend waiting for backlog to drain; suggested using their intake retry logic or temporarily increasing acknowledgement windows. They've provided incident id 9abcde and ETA unknown.

priya (handoff): ok. mitigation checklist status: alerts routed -> done, buffering logs -> done, customers notified -> done, datadog engaged -> done. Next: monitor backlog drain and assess need to failover to alternative telemetry for longer outages.

ops-automation: recommended follow-ups for postmortem: add alert on ingestion latency > 2m, add automated switch to fallback route at 3m, improve local exporter buffering to 30m retention.

priya (handoff): noted. I will keep this thread live. Assigning postmortem owner: jules.

jules (sre): will own postmortem. timeline notes saved.

sam (oncall): thanks team — passing pager.

priya (handoff): oncall taken. keeping thread open until backlog drains and errors subside. :phone: :white_check_mark:

datadog-status-bot: RESOLVED: Ingestion backlog cleared. Services should see metrics/traces resume indexing. See updates: <https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/9abcde/updates>

lin (obs): metrics are backfilling; dashboards populating for the 12:40 window. Verified traces resumed at 12:58 UTC.

priya (handoff): marking incident stabilized. We'll keep monitoring for 1 hour, then close. Postmortem owner jules to publish within 72 hours.

jules (sre): postmortem draft will include timeline, impact, decision to route to fallback, automation action items, and follow-up with Datadog contract SLA team.

support-ops: closing customer tickets where applicable, leaving note about observability gap and mitigation.

priya (handoff): closing the loop here for handoff thread. If anyone has extra logs or traces for 12:42-12:50 please attach to the postmortem doc. Thanks all. :bow:
